t: In front of you is Taxi!, a painted bronze sculpture by John Seward Johnson II. He was an American artist known for trompe-l'œil statues, which are figures made to look so lifelike they can fool the eye at a glance. That is the idea to keep in mind here: this is bronze, painted to seem like real life. Johnson was a grandson of Robert Wood Johnson the First, co-founder of Johnson and Johnson. Look closely and see how convincing the figure is before you decide whether it is a person or a statue.
